findings.text: the agreed-pass count now advances when the contract fingerprint is equal, but a fingerprint taken from an empty node-body read equals the next empty read exactly as a real contract equals itself: _node_contract_stamp reads brief and done_when from the run's node.json, and a transient read that returns {} yields brief=None and done_when=None on both passes, so two consecutive empty reads reach two agreeing passes and park a request whose stored contract is intact. The one-pass negative control and the transient test cover one empty read; a second empty read is not covered. A reading that could not read the body should not count as an agreeing reading — e.g. refuse to count a fingerprint whose body-file fields are all None (holds.py:1565-1571).
